workloads.draws: N draw(6,1,0,i%64) calls in one render pass, finish and submit once per frame
workloads.writes: N writes of bytes 1 through 16 at offset zero to one 16-byte buffer, then submit once per frame
workloads.binds: N alternating setBindGroup calls on two distinct equivalent groups, each followed by draw(6,1,0,i%64), finish and submit once per frame
workloads.rects10k: One draw(6,10000,0,0), finish and submit per frame
workloads.rects100k: One draw(6,100000,0,0), finish and submit per frame

render_target: 64x64 RGBA8Unorm; clear black alpha one; one sample; no blending
storage: 100000 48-byte rectangles; repeated 8x8 grid, x/y=tile*8+1, width/height=6, color=(1,0.5,0.25,1), radius=2
measurement: Two untimed warmup frames. Measured regions include CPU encoding/writes, finish, submit, and temporary handle destruction. Setup, queue completion waits, error checks and readback are outside the measured region. Queue completion after every frame bounds outstanding work.
correctness: Read back final buffer or every target pixel. Buffer bytes must match exactly. Pixels checked against an independent CPU rounded-rectangle distance calculation within one UNORM unit per channel. Output checksum is FNV-1a of canonical expected bytes only after every actual byte passes.
comparison: C and Silk link the same pinned Dawn archive and share untimed fixtures. Rust pins wgpu 30.0.1 and Cargo.lock; it is a backend peer, not a measure of Silk wrapper overhead.
allocation_evidence: Callgrind client markers delimit measured regions. scripts/ab saves full inclusive caller/callee trees. Attribute measured allocator calls to safe wrappers versus backend before making a no-per-call-allocation claim; wall time and source inspection alone do not establish it.
baseline_policy: bench/results/baseline.json is created only by scripts/bench --record-baseline after successful real GPU checks and measurements. No entry means no baseline measurement is claimed. Local samples and call trees live under ignored .cache/bench.
